subject: Reader and writer: comment lines and a written preamble
brief:
Support comment lines in the tabula reader and writer.

Reading. `read_rows` and `read_table` take an optional `comment` argument: a single character. A line whose first character is that marker is skipped completely, whatever it contains (quote characters too), just like a blank line. The marker only counts at the very start of a row: after other characters on the line (even a single space), and inside a quoted field (also on a later line of a field that spans lines), it is ordinary text, and a quoted field that starts with the marker is data. Without the argument (the default) no line is a comment. The marker must be exactly one character and differ from the delimiter and from the quote character; otherwise (an empty string included) raise ValueError. Line numbers in a ParseError of `read_table` keep counting every line of the text: comment lines count, so a row with the wrong number of fields that follows comment lines reports the line on which it really stands. Comment lines may also come before the header.

Writing. `write_rows` and `write_table` take the same optional `comment` argument, with the same validity rule. Edge case: when it is given, a row (the header included) whose first field begins with the marker must have that field quoted, even with minimal quoting, so that reading the text back with the same marker returns the same table; other fields that merely contain the marker are not quoted for that reason, and without the argument nothing changes. With quoting none, such a first field cannot be written and raises ValueError; quoting all still quotes every field. `write_table` also takes `preamble`, a list of text lines written before everything else, each as a comment line: the marker, one space, the text; an empty text gives the marker alone. Each of these lines ends with the chosen line ending. A preamble requires a comment marker, and a preamble line that contains a line break is refused; both raise ValueError.

All behavior that the existing tests check must keep working.
